entries.hash_note: AG-06l / audit F07 (2026-10-01). The record previously carried commit=null and hash=null while the install metadata declared a revision, so traceability was weak. Now both halves are recorded and, crucially, the audit's own caveat is honoured: a revision STRING cannot prove that the installed bytes match that commit. Verified from the live clone - the declared revision is CORRECT (git rev-parse HEAD equals it, shallow clone of the same commit) BUT the working tree does NOT match the commit: __init__.py is locally modified, 24,433 B / a56a2ebe... installed versus 23,764 B / 8e5595cb... committed, i.e. 669 bytes larger than what revision 5b9c3257 contains. No value was invented: where a fact is unknown it stays absent rather than guessed.

entries.record_note: CORRECTION 2026-10-01 (AG-06q). An earlier pass in this session reported a declared-vs-observed disagreement between this entry's lifecycle 'enabled' and its absence from the user plugins directory. That was WRONG and is withdrawn here. This entry's own type/upstream/spdx say 'bundled' (type desktop-plugin, upstream bundled, spdx bundled), which is exactly what it is: it is a BUNDLED plugin shipped with the Hermes application, not a user-installed one. It was PRESENT where it should be, so there was no disagreement to resolve and no lifecycle value needed changing. The lesson recorded: an install-shaped observation cannot be applied to a non-installed component class; the absence of a bundled plugin from the user install directory is the correct state, not a finding.
